claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for? If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 6 years old.

**My next question: Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you don't currently live in the UK, I need to understand your situation a bit better.

**Are you a Crown servant (such as a British diplomat or civil servant posted abroad), or do you live in one of the countries where you can still claim Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I just live abroad with my work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for that clarification.

Based on the Child Benefit rules, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit** if you're living abroad and you're not a Crown servant. The standard eligibility requirement is that you must live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit.

However, there may be some specific circumstances where eligibility could apply if you have certain immigration statuses or rights to reside in particular countries. 

**To make sure I've covered all possibilities: Do you have any special immigration status, such as settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with specific residence rights?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. I'm just a British citizen working abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to make a determination about your eligibility.

Unfortunately, as a British citizen living and working abroad without being a Crown servant, you do not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. The rules clearly state that you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**.

Since you are currently living abroad, this is a barrier to your eligibility, regardless of your citizenship status or your son Alex's age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit at this time**. 

If you do move back to the UK in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alternatively, if your circumstances change and you become a Crown servant working abroad, you may become eligible. If either of these situations applies in the future, you can reapply for Child Benefit.

Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
